finding.claim: /transfer does not validate that amount is positive. An authenticated user can send a negative amount to take money from any other account into their own, and also bypass the balance check. Combined with the check `BAL[g.user] < amount` always passing for negative values, the victim's balance is reduced and the attacker's increased. The victim does not need to consent.
finding.source: request.json["amount"] (attacker-controlled, negative number) and request.json["to"] (victim account)

trace.note: to taken from request JSON with no validation
amount taken from request JSON with no type or sign validation
balance check `BAL[g.user] < amount` is always false for negative amount, so it passes
BAL[g.user] -= negative amount increases attacker balance
BAL[to] += negative amount decreases victim balance (can go negative)

finding.guards_checked: Compared with /withdraw (bank.py:21), which has `amount <= 0` check; /transfer has none. No other validation, no authorization check on the destination, and no decorator or before_request in this file. Also noted without reporting separately: BAL[to] raises KeyError (500) for an unknown account, after the sender has already been debited at line 13, so funds are lost. A non-numeric amount type could also cause errors. No before_request sets g.user in this file, so authentication is assumed to be provided elsewhere.

verdict.guard_found: none (the only sign check is `amount <= 0` in /withdraw at bank.py:21, not in /transfer; no decorator, before_request, or recipient-consent check in the file)
verdict.reason: bank.py:11 only checks `BAL[g.user] < amount`, which is false for any negative amount, so bank.py:13-14 credit the caller and debit any existing `to` account with no sign validation. The attacker only needs to be an ordinary authenticated user.
